title: A Strongly Subcubic Combinatorial Algorithm for Triangle Detection with Applications

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof claims that if s is adjacent to a and exactly a is on level 1, then b and c appear on level 2 and the triangle {a,b,c} is detected when scanning b. This implicitly assumes b and c are siblings in the BFS tree. However, in a BFS, b could be discovered by another level-1 vertex before a is processed, so b and c may have different parents. Then an O(m)-time BFS that only checks simple sibling/cross-edge patterns does not necessarily detect {a,b,c}. Since Step 12 of BFS+ is not specified and the argument does not handle this BFS-order issue, the completeness proof for the main algorithm is invalid.

predicted_errors.error_location: Time analysis of Phase I / Theorem 2 runtime bounds
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The algorithm uses 'the adjacency matrix of G' for O(1) edge tests, but the runtime analysis omits the Ω(n²) cost of constructing that matrix. Under the standard adjacency-list input model, if m=O(n), the claimed O(m^{2/3}n)=O(n^{5/3}) and O(mn^{1/2})=O(n^{3/2}) bounds are smaller than the n² preprocessing cost. Thus the parameterized running-time claims are not valid as stated unless an alternative O(1) edge-query structure is built.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 'Running time in terms of m', paragraph after Lemma 1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states: 'First, consider TRIANGLE-DETECTION-1... Phase I takes O(mx) time... With the setting x ∼ n^{1/2}... O(mn^{1/2}) overall.' But TRIANGLE-DETECTION-1 sets x←⌊m^{1/3}⌋ and has Phase I time O(nx²). The O(mx) and x∼n^{1/2} analysis belongs to TRIANGLE-DETECTION-2. This paragraph contradicts the earlier algorithm definitions.

The paper defines T_3(m) as the time to find a triangle in a graph with m edges, then applies T_3(n) for n segments and claims replacing BMM with Theorem 2 gives O(n^{4/3}). But the intersection graph of n segments can have Θ(n²) edges; applying O(m^{4/3}) to m=n² gives O(n^{8/3}), not O(n^{4/3}). No reduction to an O(n)-edge graph is described, so the stated bound conflates the number of segments/vertices with the number of edges and is unsupported.
